diagnosis.summary: Ingest failed because upstream renamed customers.country to country_code in the 2026-10-01 file. Ingest config has no mapping, so the schema check rejected it. I proposed apply_column_mapping(customers, country_code -> country), which is the runbook fix for a rename with the same meaning.

root_cause.explanation: The 2026-10-01 customers.csv header has country_code where the contract expects country. The 2026-09-30 file matched the contract. Ingest config is empty, so there is no mapping. The other four columns are unchanged and in the same order, and the visible values are 2-letter codes as before.

evidence.claim: Ingest failed on a schema mismatch: country is missing and country_code is unexpected.
The header changed on 10-01 only. 09-30 matched the contract, and no other columns differ. Only 4 of the 30 rows were inspected, and all were US.
No column mapping exists in the ingest config.
The runbook says to map a same-meaning rename at ingest and to escalate if the meaning changes.

alternatives_considered: request_upstream_redelivery: the rename looks deliberate and persistent, so a re-export would likely carry the same header.
ignore_extra_columns: it can't supply the missing contract column, so it wouldn't fix the rename.
escalate_to_owner (upstream_app_team): only needed if the meaning changed. The visible values look like the same 2-letter codes, but the sample was small.
rerun_only: nothing has changed, so it would fail the same way.

proposal.rationale: Upstream renamed customers.country to country_code in the 2026-10-01 file. The column is in the same position, holds the same 2-letter codes, and no other columns differ. The runbook says to map a same-meaning rename at ingest.

applied: ingest now reads raw.customers.country from upstream column 'country_code'
